deities: Goddess Durga (Bhagavathi) in three forms: Vana Durga, Bhadrakali and Jala Durga
festivals: Annual 14-15 day festival in Meenam (March) - tribal chiefs perform the Kodiyettu flag-hoisting on the 7th day; nightly Kalamezhuthu ritual art; Oppana Varavu procession; Rudhirakkolam symbolic fight between Durga and Darika

history.period: 14th century (one local source says 13th century; founding date unverified)
history.summary: Legend traces the shrine to a Kodungallur (Cranganore) temple priest travelling to Thirunelli who rested near the Kabini river and lost the goddess's anklet and sword; a Paniya tribesman found them caught in a creeper on a sacred fig tree, and a divine voice declared the goddess present here in three forms - Vana Durga, Jala Durga and Bhadrakali. The Kottayam Raja, then camping in Wayanad, ordered a temple built; the name comes from 'valliyoor amma' ('Mother, disentangle thyself'). British records called it the 'Fish Pagoda' for its architecture. It is a major tribal festival centre of Wayanad; the annual March festival is hoisted by tribal chiefs. CSV ERROR FLAG: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name - this temple is in KERALA, and the actual nearest town is Mananthavady (CSV town 'Wayanad' is the district, not the town; verify). DATE CONFLICT FLAG: local sources variously date the shrine to the 13th or 14th century and the festival to 13, 14 or 15 days (Meenam 1-14); treat dates as unverified.

name: Valliyoorkavu Bhagavathi Temple
town_description: Mananthavady is a town in the Wayanad district of Kerala, on the banks of the Kabini river. It serves as a gateway to northern Wayanad's tribal heritage sites and forest attractions, including the Valliyoorkavu Bhagavathi Temple about 3 km away.
